question.prompt:
The table shown displays the grade distribution of the \(30\) students in a mathematics class on the last two tests. For example, exactly one student received a ‘D’ on Test \(1\) and a ‘C’ on Test \(2\) (the circled entry). What percent of the students received the same grade on both tests?

[Figure 1](figures/1986_AMC_8_Q12_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
The rows give Test \(1\) grades and the columns give Test \(2\) grades. A student received the same grade twice exactly when the row and column labels match. Therefore we use the cells for \((A,A)\), \((B,B)\), \((C,C)\), \((D,D)\), and \((F,F)\).

These cells contain
\[
2+4+5+1+0=12
\]
students. Each student belongs to exactly one cell, so this sum counts every student with matching grades once. The circled entry has different row and column grades, so it is not included.

Dividing this count by the total of \(30\) students gives the required percentage:
\[
\frac{12}{30}=0.4=\boxed{40\%}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\text{D}\).
solutions.title: Count matching-grade cells
